**Mann:** And that's how it happened — I swear it on my paycheck, and the responsibilities that come with it.

**Lipphart:** Weren't you bemoaning how little you make as a doorman?

**Mann:** I'm not just any doorman. I oversee demolition work and cultural heritage preservation.

**Mann:** Though yeah, the pay is bad... Well, then I swear it on my reputation at the tavern.

**Huffman:** A most serious oath for us Mondstadters.

**Huffman:** I should really investigate this myself, but I still have to meet up with the Knights' expedition, who are returning to Dornman Port...

**Huffman:** Sorry about this, Traveler, but could you check out the sanatorium for me?

**Paimon:** Ugh, kinda-sorta scary stories like this usually mean something bigger's at play.

**Lipphart:** Then what about super scary stories?

**Paimon:** The truth behind those is usually... Uh... basic scientific facts about how superstition can be harmful.

- **Traveler:** It's fine. I know my way around a fight either way.

**Paimon:** Eh, true. We've run into ghosts before, too. Most of them were actually pretty easy to talk to.

**Mann:** So there really are ghosts in this world?

**Paimon:** No, no. It's all just strange elemental powers and scientific phenomena at work.

**Lipphart:** In that case, I won't go today. I'll just stay in Dornman Port and have some drinks.

#### Investigate the tombstone

**Paimon:** It's as we thought. There's nothing in the graveyard.

**Paimon:** Old Mann must've made a mistake...

**Paimon:** Still, look at the portrait on this grave. This girl was so young... There's a sad story behind this one for sure.

**???:** Are you friends of my sister too?

**Paimon:** Eek!

- **Traveler:** You look... exactly the same.

**Paimon:** S—Sister...?

**Paimon:** Uh, so, you've gotta be the younger sister of the person buried here, right?

**???:** Well, are you also her friends?

- **Traveler:** I... don't think we count.

**Paimon:** You scared the old man at the gate last night, so the Knights sent us to investigate.

**???:** I see. Well, I'm just here to look for her. I didn't expect that rumor to be true.

**Paimon:** A rumor?

**???:** That "those who go to the sanatorium will stay there," or something similar.

**???:** In her letters, my sister said the sanatorium was about to close, and that she was going somewhere far away.

**Paimon:** Um... M—Maybe she went traveling around the world or something?

**Paimon:** No wait. Her gravestone is right here... Sorry.

**???:** It's alright. Before I came, I thought the same way you did. It took me some time to prepare myself before I could come here for answers.

**???:** I might have arrived a bit too late last night and ended up frightening the old man.

**???:** Please help me pass along my apology. I'm sorry for causing all this trouble.

**Paimon:** It's okay. Paimon totally gets you. Just gotta explain it to everyone, and you'll be fine.

**???:** It was a little late last night. I'd planned to ask the old man about the situation, but he fled without even looking back.

**???:** For now, I want to look for traces of how she lived her life. Perhaps that would lead us to some clues on... why she would...

**Paimon:** Y'know what? Let us help you. It's getting late, and the sooner we finish, the sooner we can head down the mountain.

**Paimon:** Right, Traveler?

**Paimon:** By the way, what's your name?

**???:** Ah...

**???:** ...

**Paimon:** Wh—What is it? Is it an, uh, embarrassing name or something?

**Paimon:** In that case, Paimon can, uh, give you a nickname... How's that sound?

**???:** No. It's just... I had planned to... Well, I came to say goodbye.

**???:** Hmm...

**Zeitlind:** Zeitlind. My name is Zeitlind.

**Paimon:** Alright then. Let's help Zeitlind look around together, shall we, Traveler?

**Zeitlind:** A cursed mountain where none who enter ever return...

**Paimon:** Um, what exactly are we looking for?

**Zeitlind:** Maybe a note. A scrap of paper... Or perhaps just traces of a life that once existed here.

**Zeitlind:** With the demolition already this far along, there may not be much left to find. Still, I have to try.

#### Talk to Zeitlind

#### Look for the traces left by Zeitlind's older sister

**Paimon:** There's so much dust on the bed. It must've been meant for sanatorium patients back in the day, right?

#### Look for the traces left by Zeitlind's older sister

**Paimon:** Zeitlind, were you waiting for us here?

**Zeitlind:** No. I think... Something feels off...

**Zeitlind:** Uh... was that always so far away?

**Paimon:** Huh? This place looks kinda different from before.

- **Traveler:** (What happened here...?)

**Paimon:** Whoa!

**Nihilita:** I am Nihilita, Watcher of Nothingness, the Open-Eyed.

**Nihilita:** Noble traveler from distant realms, returnee from the sea of stars... Greetings. I bid you welcome.

**Zeitlind:** It... knows you?

- **Traveler:** But I don't know it.

**Nihilita:** As it should be. We dwell within the watchtowers of the world. We were never meant to meet, even across countless ages.

**Nihilita:** Yet I have now fallen into the mortal realm, for one purpose alone. I beg that you ascend to the high heavens and free the Aiones of the past from their inverted fates.

**Nihilita:** Please, touch the Anemo Archon's statue over there. It is a gateway that leads unto the heavens.

**Paimon:** Wait! Can't you see that there's an ordinary person here?

**Paimon:** Are you sure Zeitlind is supposed to hear these things? At least let us take her back first!

**Nihilita:** ...

**Nihilita:** Inconceivable. You really came...

**Zeitlind:** Ah!

**Nihilita:** Please remain calm. I merely placed her under my protection, so that she shall not suffer any apathic afflictions after ascending.

**Paimon:** So, you mean we're bringing Zeitlind with us?

**Nihilita:** She has her own journey to embark upon. When you reach the temple above the sky, she will be restored.

**Paimon:** Hey, hold on! We never agreed to go to some strange place like that. Let Zeitlind out first!

**Nihilita:** This is not some strange place. It is the seat of governance above the skies. Its name is "Segment-Domain Tau." Or perhaps, let us use its lost name.

**Nihilita:** The Temple of Space.

- **Traveler:** The Temple of Space...

- **Traveler:** (And what it just did earlier...)

**Nihilita:** That is correct. It belongs to the god who once appeared before you, my creator. Within the temple, you shall find your answers.

**Nihilita:** Please take this with you. It will aid you in my stead.

**Paimon:** Ah! What is this thing?

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** It's kind of cute.

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** A little strange, but kind of cute.

##### Shared continuation

**Paimon:** Uh, could you explain what it actually is!?

**Nihilita:** A Watcher does not explain. A Watcher observes, in silence.

**Nihilita:** Once safety may be guaranteed, it will restore Zeitlind.

**Paimon:** Don't just assume that we're going! You're just looking to dump responsibility for this onto someone, aren't you?

**Nihilita:** Noble outlander, are you willing to go?

**Paimon:** There it is again, talking to yourself and dodging the question. You haven't been making any sense for a while now, y'know?

**Paimon:** Traveler, do you know what it's trying to say?

- **Traveler:** The Temple of Space...

- **Traveler:** I will go.

**Paimon:** Eh!?

**Paimon:** Okay, sure. If that's what you want, then Paimon will go with you.

**Paimon:** Huh? Where did it go?

**Nihilita:** If my earlier discourtesy has stirred anger within you, come at me with blade in hand. I will await you in the mortal world.

**???:** !

**Paimon:** Zeitlind! Are you alright?

**Zeitlind:** Mm. I'm fine. My sense of time's a bit off, though. Like a very long while has passed, and yet also just an instant.

- **Traveler:** That sounds like a familiar feeling.

**Zeitlind:** You've felt this way before?

**Zeitlind:** You must've been through plenty of misfortune, too. How long has it been for you, then?

- **Traveler:** About... five hundred years?

**Zeitlind:** What? Has so much time passed already?

**Paimon:** Oh, no. He's talking about the time-weirdness stuff that happened to him. / Oh, no. She's talking about the time-weirdness stuff that happened to her.

**Paimon:** That said, Paimon's not sure if "five hundred years" is that accurate at this point either.

**Paimon:** As for this time, it's only been about ten minutes or so?

**Zeitlind:** Huh. So that's how long it's been?

- **Traveler:** Say...

**Zeitlind:** Hmm?

- **Traveler:** You never asked us for our names.

**Zeitlind:** Ah, yes. When I tried to call for help just now, I realized I didn't even know what to call you.

**Zeitlind:** Sorry. At first, I was planning to... Well, never mind.

**Zeitlind:** I already know that you're Traveler. What about your pet?

**Paimon:** Hey! Paimon's not a pet! Paimon's Traveler's best guide and companion!

- **Traveler:** Yes, Paimon's not a pet.

**Paimon:** And if you're gonna make another corny joke, you can stuff it.

**Zeitlind:** Oh. I'm sorry, Paimon.

**Zeitlind:** Well then. Hello, Paimon. Hello Traveler.

**Paimon:** We'll make sure you get back down safely. But for now, we don't have any leads as to how.

**Paimon:** So let's keep moving forward. We need to find someone and ask them what's going on.

#### Talk to the strange person

**Paimon:** Hello!

**???:** Huh!? Humans...? I thought the "uplifting" had already ended. More cases like Hilda's, then?

**???:** No, wait. Perhaps you were simply unlucky. Newcomers who have only recently passed the trial of the Apathic Interval, maybe?

**Istoria:** Greetings, newcomers. My name is Istoria. I hail from the age when the Dark Dragon King rent the sky open. And you are?

**Paimon:** What sorta age was that?

- **Traveler:** Anyway, call me Traveler.

**Paimon:** Paimon's Paimon.

**Zeitlind:** Zeitlind.

**Istoria:** Hmm. So, you're Zeitlind.

**Dex:** !

**Istoria:** Ah. Dexter. You are here as well!

**Istoria:** Now I understand. You must be people of the present age. In which case, you have come to reinforce us!

**Paimon:** That was quick!

**Paimon:** Also, Dex's real name is Dexter, huh? Is it your friend?

**Istoria:** No. We call it Dex too. But it just sent me a secret signal.

**Istoria:** As such, I introduced it using the more official, more impressive-sounding name.

**Paimon:** Hey, Hey, Traveler. Paimon wants a formal name and a secret code, too.

**Istoria:** Ah, but now is not the time for such talk.

**Istoria:** Since Nihilita has sent you up here, that means it is finally our time to strike back.

**Paimon:** Wait a minute! We're still confused.

**Istoria:** How confused? More confused than I was the first time I looked upon Escher's paintings?

- **Traveler:** E...scher? As in, Escher the Engineer?

**Istoria:** Does the name ring a bell? He's from a very long time ago, though. Surely not someone you know...

**Istoria:** Eh, you know what? Who knows. Maybe he really was famous. Actually, that pisses me off. Why didn't I make my mark in history?

**Istoria:** You know what? Let's just call him "Maukie" from now on.

- **Traveler:** Escher?

**Istoria:** Just an unlucky, ill-natured painter.

**Istoria:** His family calls him "Maukie", and so do we.

**Paimon:** "Maukie"... Paimon feels like she might've heard that before...

**Istoria:** Ach. No, no. This isn't the time for that either.

**Istoria:** Let me ask you, do any of you have combat strength on par with a junior Remurian Centurion or higher?

**Paimon:** Don't worry, Traveler can beat people up just fine.

**Istoria:** Come on, then. Let's head out and show them what Pankration, or maybe Machaira, means to you.

**Zeitlind:** ...

#### Go to the center of the Pillar Hall of Space

#### Go to the center of the Pillar Hall of Space

#### Talk to Istoria

**Istoria:** Ah, yes. Come, come, it's team huddle time. We've a strategy meeting to hold.

**Zeitlind:** Does the team include me?

**Paimon:** Ooh, Paimon almost forgot. Istoria, do you know how to send someone back down to the ground?

**Istoria:** I do.

**Paimon:** Then can you tell us how to send Zeitlind back? She's just an ordinary person.

**Istoria:** In the past, that would have been nearly impossible. But the temple's laws and order draw close unto collapse, making it now a trivial matter.

**Istoria:** You simply need to do me a small favor.

**Paimon:** Hmm, alright, but it better be small.

**Istoria:** Oh, it's simple. Smash a few crappy guards, rescue an old friend, and escort us back to the center of the Pillar Hall.

**Paimon:** That doesn't sound too bad.

**Paimon:** And do you know what kind of god rules this place? Traveler is looking for her.

**Istoria:** This was once the sacred hall of the God of Space. But she is nowhere to be found.

**Istoria:** After the mistress vanished, one of the two stewards fell from grace and departed.

**Istoria:** The one who remained, Melanta, grew increasingly severe with us. He did not descend into the mortal world, but he has descended into madness.

**Paimon:** Melanta? Does that mean that the one who fell from grace is that self-absorbed Nihilita guy?

**Istoria:** Correct. The Watcher who introduced Dex to you is one who departed. Nihilita of Nothingness.

**Paimon:** Hah, so it really was that big-winged guy who talks to himself, doesn't care what people say, and changes the subject whenever you ask him uncomfortable questions!

**Istoria:** Huh. Does he really talk that much?

**Istoria:** *sigh* No matter. The two of them were once divine familiars who watched over the world from the Pillar Hall of Space.

**Istoria:** The Temple of Space selects people and objects from a specific historical age or a now-vanished civilization, using them as the smallest possible segments.

**Istoria:** Once elevated, the chosen are preserved here as living memories, forever.

**Zeitlind:** That doesn't sound like a very happy fate.

**Istoria:** I suspect it was not originally designed as an eternal paradise or some heaven in the sky.

**Istoria:** Still, the God of Space's sisters would occasionally bring things of interest into the temple and grant small pardons for acts of change.

**Paimon:** Oh, Paimon gets it. This place was a spotless but dull bookshelf that the sisters then covered in stickers and stuffed with light novels.

**Istoria:** Then Melanta, driven by longing for his creator, reversed all the rules to their original form. He began purging everything that had changed, punishing anyone who broke from precedent.

**Istoria:** I gathered the courage to leave the relative safety of the temple's center, hoping I might be able to save an old friend.

**Istoria:** But my lack of Pankration training caught up with me, and I ended up getting chased by the guards and hiding in that spot earlier.

**Paimon:** Alright. That's the introduction. What's our plan?

**Istoria:** We fight our way through and save anyone we know.

**Paimon:** Fine. Looks like Melanta's the highest up the ladder we can reach for now. Hopefully, we can get some answers from him.

**Zeitlind:** It's beautiful...

**Istoria:** Look. That is the center of the Pillar Hall of Space.

**Istoria:** Now then. Let us set our course for the heart of the world. A realm unreserved for the old or the young, rulers or fools.

#### Continue onward

#### Defeat the Keepers

#### Restore the display case and free the trapped person

#### Talk to the trapped person

**Istoria:** Well, well. If it isn't our great master of anti-self-termination, Josephus. So, why are you here, cursing all who live?

**Josephus:** Cut it out. Nobody dies in the Temple of Space.

**Istoria:** How strange. Did you try testing that rule, Sir Anti-Self-Termination?

**Josephus:** Keep talking, and a new batch of guards will be on its way.

**Istoria:** Alright. Special times call for special treatment. I won't make fun of you.

**Istoria:** Traveler, Zeitlind. This is Josephus. He's a friend of mine.

**Josephus:** No need to be so sentimental. Everyone here is everyone else's friend.

**Josephus:** If you can't come to love or be loved by everyone over such long periods of time, you'd drown the world in sorrow.

**Josephus:** Come. Let us set our course for the heart of the world. A realm not reserved for the old or the dead, for the rich or poor.

**Istoria:** Hehe, I've quoted that poem before.

#### Talk to your companions

**Josephus:** It's safer here. I don't know why, but the suppression-type guards can't get in.

**Istoria:** Organization-type Keepers usually don't harm people either. Unless you try to steal relics, that is.

**Paimon:** Zeitlind, you've been gripping that suitcase this whole time. Your knuckles are all pale.

**Paimon:** It's safe here, so just put it down for now, 'kay?

**Paimon:** Well, unless you've got stolen relics in that suitcase. But that can't be, right?

**Zeitlind:** Mhm.

**Paimon:** Still, Paimon's sure it's gotta be full of valuable items.

**Zeitlind:** Not really. Just some things I needed to say goodbye to before leaving.

**Paimon:** Huh?

**Zeitlind:** It's nothing.

**Istoria:** You and your sister have vastly different personalities.

**Zeitlind:** What did you say!?

**Zeitlind:** Ah... I mean... Have you... met my sister? Did she come here before? So the "Hilda" you mentioned before really is...

**Istoria:** Easy now, young Zeitlind. This place is safe. We can take our time talking about your sister.

**Josephus:** Shameless fellow. Hilda called you Grandpa.

**Istoria:** I couldn't tell you how many years ago I was born. Still, I have heard you all speak of an age long past, when the gods waged war across the land.

**Istoria:** In my time, there were no gods living in our lands at all. Have you ever seen an angel?

**Raumhilda:** That makes you a great-great-great-great grandpa, Grandpa Istoria!

**Istoria:** Nay, nay. Once you get here, all are caught within stagnant space-time. Saints and commoners, wise and foolish, young and old. There is no difference.

**Istoria:** That is to say, don't call me Grandpa.

**Raumhilda:** Then let's call each other whatever we want. I'll call you "Grandpa Istoria," and you can call me "young Hilda."

**Istoria:** She was a good lass. But for some reason, she always looked a little gloomy.

**Josephus:** Indeed.

**Paimon:** Hey, stop getting sentimental! Zeitlind's suitcase has been stolen!

**Zeitlind:** Hey, give it back!

**Josephus:** It got away. This is going to be a difficult chase.

**Zeitlind:** Wh—What do we do...

**Istoria:** Don't let this get you down, Zeitlind. I have a theory.

**Istoria:** Traveler, come with me.

#### Retrieve Zeitlind's suitcase

#### Defeat the Keepers

#### Defeat the Keepers

**Istoria:** There it is.

**Zeitlind:** Oh, thank goodness!

**Paimon:** Looks like we've only recovered a small part of Lind's stuff, though.

**Istoria:** Then it's as I suspected. Your suitcase and everything inside it have been classified as relics of this age.

**Istoria:** The rest were likely dispersed and placed in other areas.

**Paimon:** Don't worry, Zeitlind. We'll find them together.

**Zeitlind:** ...Thank you all.

**Istoria:** Then, shall I tell you about the themed areas?

**Paimon:** Okay then, tell us.

- **Traveler:** I'm listening.

**Istoria:** Besides people like us, some landscapes, relics, and even ecosystems were also uplifted to this place.

**Istoria:** The temple was originally meant to preserve them as segments of human culture, though some gradually developed their own functions.

**Istoria:** Take, for example, the Luyang Academy from ancient Liyue. It has now become an area devoted to art and painting.

**Istoria:** Then there's Venipi, a laborer who once hauled stone for The Mausoleum of King Deshret. Under orders, he rebuilt a desert style complex called the Desert Pavilion.

**Istoria:** Last is my personal favorite, the Mahavaipulya Chamber. Besides ancient texts, it also contains new novels written by some of the uplifted.

**Istoria:** But since the purpose of the Temple of Space is preservation rather than evolution, they were also the first to face punishment.

**Paimon:** So if we go to those three places, we can find the things Zeitlind lost, right?

**Istoria:** You could also free those areas and rescue the others. If it's not too much trouble, of course.

**Paimon:** Oh ho, Istoria. That's gonna run you extra.

**Zeitlind:** I wouldn't put it like that. We should go help everyone *and* find my things along the way.

**Istoria:** Your personal effects are of utmost importance here, Lind. You are, after all, someone who lives in the present.

**Istoria:** This place is but an anthology of the past. It has no future, whereas you still have yours.

**Istoria:** That makes your needs the most important. Do you understand?

**Zeitlind:** In the end, a living person may amount to nothing more than a name on gravestone.

**Istoria:** Even so, a name carries countless memories, as well as the stories and strength passed on through them, young Zeitlind.

**Istoria:** Let us return and rest for now. I suspect you still have many questions.

**???:** Some people just won't listen. I already told you, now's not the time to go up the mountain.

**Huffman:** Easy there, Old Mann. Let's calm down and talk this out.

**???:** We were getting along just fine earlier at the Night Brew.

**???:** But the moment I mentioned I was heading for Windrest Peak, he grabbed me and dragged me all the way here.

**Paimon:** Oh, Huffman. What's going on here?

**Huffman:** As you can see, Old Mann is trying his best to keep people away from Windrest Peak.

**Huffman:** Anyway, let me introduce you. This is Lipphart, an adventurer.

**Mann:** What I saw... What I felt... It was terrifying! Surely you don't wish to hear it?

**Lipphart:** Doesn't look like I'm going anywhere today, so let's hear it. Consider it an extension of our drinking and bragging session from earlier.

**Lipphart:** So, what sort of "great peril" are we facing here?

**Mann:** The sanatorium's haunted! Seriously! I saw them ghosts with my own eyes!

**Paimon:** Ghosts!?

**Mann:** It happened last night...
